formation.title: The Swargadeo's Mandate Restored
formation.text:
Six centuries since Sukaphaa led his Tai band over the Patkai passes into the Brahmaputra valley, the Swargadeo's banner is raised again over Charaideo. The maidam mounds of seventeen kings stand untouched on the ridge above us. The paik bells ring across the valley calling every household to service. The seven Borgohain offices await their charters, the Borphukan rides out toward Guwahati, and the namghars of Sankardev's disciples are filling with gathered villagers. The Mughals battered themselves seventeen times against this kingdom and broke; now we choose what shape the unconquered realm will take.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

modifiers.name: Swargadeo's Mandate
modifiers.text: The Tai-Ahom restoration: paik corvee, Buranji court, the seven great offices, and the riding tradition of dragoon nobility: the unconquered realm of Sukaphaa's heirs.

modifiers.name: Eka-Sarana Dharma
modifiers.text: Sankardev's neo-Vaishnavism as the kingdom's organizing principle: namghar in every village, satra at every district, devotion accessible to all castes and the hill peoples alike.

advances.name: The Paik System
advances.text: The corvee labor institution that organized every adult Ahom male into a got of four and assigned each to one of the great offices. The kingdom's militia, its public works, and its tax base all derive from the paik.

event.title: The Paik Roll
event.text: Every adult man in the valley owes service. The Borgohain ministers have completed the great paik census: each household contributes one paik to the state, organized into got of three or four men, assigned to one of the great offices. Three paiks support the fourth in the field. The militia of the kingdom, its labor for road and dyke and dockyard, and its tax base all derive from this single institution. With the rolls codified, no Swargadeo will rule without knowing the strength of his realm to the man.

options.text: The paik system is the spine of the kingdom

modifiers.name: Paik Codified
modifiers.text: Every adult male in the rolls, every got of four assigned to its office, every dyke and road and dockyard built by paik labor: the kingdom mobilized to the household.

advances.name: Buranji Chronicles
advances.text: The court chronicle tradition begun under Sukaphaa, written first in Tai-Ahom and later in Assamese, one of the great historiographies of South Asia and the documentary backbone of dynastic continuity.

event.title: The Buranjis of the Court
event.text: The court historians have completed the latest volume of the Buranji, chronicling the reigns of the Swargadeos, the embassies received, the wars fought, the lineages of the great offices. Written first in the Tai-Ahom script and now translated into Assamese, the Buranjis are the kingdom's memory. Few states in South Asia keep records as systematic as ours; few rulers can speak with the authority of six centuries of documented dynastic continuity. The court orders the chronicles formally codified and copies sent to every satra.

options.text: The Buranjis preserve the realm's memory

modifiers.name: Buranji Court
modifiers.text: Six centuries of documented dynastic continuity, copied into every satra and quoted in every diplomatic exchange, a state with longer memory than any of its rivals.

advances.name: Charaideo Maidams
advances.text: The royal mound necropolis at Charaideo where Tai-derived burial tradition continued through six centuries of Ahom kings, the spiritual heart of the kingdom and the legitimating site of every coronation.

advances.name: The Seven Great Offices
advances.text: Burhagohain, Borgohain, Borpatrogohain, Borphukan, Borbarua and the lesser offices, a council nobility that balanced royal authority and administered the kingdom from Charaideo to Guwahati.

advances.name: Hill Auxiliaries
advances.text: Garo, Naga, Bodo, and Kachari fighters drawn into Ahom service through paid alliance and corvee exemption, masters of the jungle terrain that broke every invading army.

advances.name: The Brahmaputra Fleet
advances.text: Bachari and kosa: light gun-armed riverboats forming the patrol fleet that controlled the Brahmaputra's bends and choke points under the Borphukan's command.

advances.name: Namghar Network
advances.text: Sankardev's neo-Vaishnava prayer hall, the village-level institution of the Eka-Sarana religion that bound hill, valley, and river under shared devotional ritual.

advances.name: The Eka-Sarana Movement
advances.text: Srimanta Sankardev's bhakti reform: devotion to one God in vernacular Assamese, accessible without Brahmin priests, drawing in tribal and lower-caste worshippers alike.

event.title: The Bhakti of Srimanta Sankardev
event.text: Srimanta Sankardev has come down from the Mahapurusha pilgrimage with the Eka-Sarana: devotion to one God, accessible without Brahmin priests, sung in Assamese in the namghars of every village. The satras are filling with disciples. The Brahmin orthodoxy at our court calls it heresy. The Bodo and Kachari peoples find a path into our religion that does not require they abandon their gods. The Swargadeo must rule on what Eka-Sarana means for the kingdom.

modifiers.name: Official Vaishnavism
modifiers.text: Eka-Sarana as state religion: namghar attendance compulsory, satra patronage central, the hill peoples drawn into the Sanskritized fold.

options.text: Let the namghars stand beside the old shrines

modifiers.name: Religious Pluralism
modifiers.text: Tai shrines, Saiva temples, Vaishnava namghars, and tribal sacred groves all under the Swargadeo's protection: the religion of the realm is the religion of every village.

advances.name: Tai Dragoons
advances.text: Mounted infantry of the Ahom court, descendants of the Tai cavalry tradition that crossed the Patkai with Sukaphaa, the elite striking arm of the realm.

advances.name: Saraighat Doctrine
advances.text: Lachit Borphukan's naval-and-land tactics that destroyed the Mughal fleet at Saraighat in 1671: coordinated bachari ambush, riverbank artillery, and elite marine assault.

event.title: Lachit Borphukan on the Brahmaputra
event.text: Ram Singh's Mughal armada lies anchored off Saraighat. Lachit Borphukan, dying of fever and carried in a litter, has refused to retreat. Tonight the Borphukan calls his commanders together: should the bachari fleet ambush the Mughal warships at the river bend where the Brahmaputra narrows, or should we burn our own villages, retreat into the hills, and let monsoon and jungle do the killing? The Mughals have never lost a campaign, but they have also never fought in our country.

options.text: Strike at the river bend: let the Brahmaputra be their grave

modifiers.name: Lachit's River Doctrine
modifiers.text: The Brahmaputra is our wall. The bachari fleet patrols the bends; the riverine cannon answers from the fortified banks; no Mughal armada will pass.

options.text: Burn the valley: let the jungle and monsoon kill them

modifiers.name: Jungle Resistance
modifiers.text: Burnt villages, withdrawn population, hill ambushes, monsoon attrition: the invader fights mosquitoes and starvation more than soldiers.

advances.name: Dolakharia Dockyard
advances.text: The Borphukan's naval headquarters at Guwahati, the river fortress and shipyard controlling the Brahmaputra mouth where the kingdom met the Mughal frontier.

advances.name: Satra Monasteries
advances.text: Sankardev's institutional successors: monastic complexes that became economic, cultural, and political powers in their own right, repositories of manuscript scholarship and Vaishnava reform.

advances.name: Seventeen Invasions Repulsed
advances.text: From Turbak's raid in 1532 through the Mughal campaigns of the 1660s and 1670s, every imperial expedition into Assam broke against jungle, monsoon, and the Borphukan's defenses.

advances.name: Brahmaputra Command
advances.text: The river as logistics highway and barrier, enabling rapid Ahom movement, denying enemies supply, and binding the valley together where roads could not reach.

advances.name: Jaibanmar Artillery
advances.text: The Ahom heavy gunnery corps, blending Indian and Persian designs into field and riverine artillery: swivel guns on warships, jaiban cannon in fortified positions.

advances.name: Rudra Singha's Paik Reform
advances.text: Rudra Singha's restructuring of the corvee system formalizing military service, public works obligation, and revenue assessment in a single integrated institution.

advances.name: Muga Silk Cultivation
advances.text: Assam's golden silk, produced from the Antheraea assamensis silkworm, a textile unique to the Brahmaputra valley and the kingdom's most distinctive luxury export.

advances.name: Chronicle Codification
advances.text: The court historians' formal codification of the Buranjis under Rudra Singha, fixing dynastic and administrative records as the legitimating documentary corpus of the realm.

advances.name: Modern Paltan Drill
advances.text: European-influenced infantry drill blended with paik recruitment, the modernizing reforms adopted in the late Ahom period to face firearm-equipped Burmese and British armies.

advances.name: Assam Tea Cultivation
advances.text: The singular crop that came to define the Brahmaputra valley's modern economy, tea plantations developed first under Ahom patronage and later expanded by colonial planters.

advances.name: The Borphukan's Viceroyalty
advances.text: The viceroyal governance of Lower Assam from Guwahati, balancing the Swargadeo's court at Rangpur and Charaideo and managing the Mughal frontier.

advances.name: Swargadeo's Court
advances.text: The absolutist evolution of Ahom kingship under Rudra Singha and Siva Singha, with formal court ceremony, codified law, and patronized Sanskritic high culture.

advances.name: Anti-Burmese Resistance
advances.text: The brutal Burmese occupation of 1817 to 1826 broke the kingdom but forged a vernacular Assamese identity in resistance, partisan defense binding hill and valley anew.

advances.name: Assamese Cultural Revival
advances.text: Vernacular literature, sattriya dance from the satras, and the synthesis of Tai, Bodo, Kachari, and Sanskritic traditions into a unified Assamese cultural identity.

advances.name: Brahmaputra Industry
advances.text: Late-period modernization of the river economy with mills, dockyards, and textile works on the Brahmaputra's banks.

advances.name: Modernized Paltan Levy
advances.text: The paik corvee system updated to raise European-drilled line infantry, the synthesis of six centuries of Ahom recruitment and modern military doctrine.

destiny.name: The Unconquered Realm
destiny.text: Six centuries of Tai-Ahom rule, seventeen Mughal invasions repulsed. The Swargadeo's choice between imperial reach and devotional federation will define what this kingdom becomes.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: The Destiny Chosen
event.text: The Borgohain ministers gather at Charaideo to read the chronicles of the choice just made. The court historians prepare new Buranji volumes; the maidam priests consecrate fresh ground for the kings yet to come; the Borphukan rides east to sound the paik bells. The unconquered kingdom begins its second age.

destiny.name: Push to the Surma Valley
destiny.text: Cross the Brahmaputra delta and seize the lower Bengal frontier. Take Sylhet on the Surma and Mymensingh on the Old Brahmaputra to break out of the Assamese basin and into Bengal proper. Guwahati, the gate of the valley, is built up as the base of every campaign down the river.

conditions.text: Chose the Swargadeo's Tai mandate
Own Sylhet, or a subject owns it
Own Mymensingh, or a subject owns it
Guwahati is ours and has reached 24 development

event.title: The Surma and the Old Brahmaputra
event.text: Sylhet has fallen, Mymensingh fallen, the lower Bengal frontier is held by Ahom paiks for the first time in our history. The chronicle says no Tai-Ahom Swargadeo has ever ruled west of the Brahmaputra delta. The chronicle is now wrong. The Husayn Shahi governors retreat to Gaur, dispatching letters of alarm to Delhi. The kingdom has crossed into Bengal.

destiny.name: Seize Bengal's Capitals
destiny.text: The Husayn Shahi seats fall before the paik militia. Take Gaur on the Ganges and Sonargaon on the Meghna, the twin capitals of medieval Bengal, and open a Paik Office in each, so that the conquered country is entered on the rolls and its men answer the Swargadeo's call as the valley's do.

conditions.text: Own Gaur, or a subject owns it
Own Sonargaon, or a subject owns it
A Paik Office stands in our Gaur and in our Sonargaon

event.title: Gaur Falls, Sonargaon Submits
event.text: Husayn Shahi authority breaks. Gaur, the great Ganges capital, is occupied; Sonargaon on the Meghna submits to Borgohain governance. The Buranji historians begin a new chapter: the kingdom of Sukaphaa now rules from the Patkai to the lower Ganges. The Borgohain council debates how to hold the conquest. Should the paik corvee be extended to the new districts, mobilizing every Bengali household into the imperial machine? Or should the Borgohain offices be transplanted whole, governing through the existing Bengali nobility?

options.text: Extend paik corvee: every household serves the imperium

modifiers.name: Paik Imperium
modifiers.text: Every household in conquered Bengal entered onto the paik rolls: the corvee system extended continentally, the imperial machine mobilized to the village.

options.text: Transplant Borgohain governance through the local nobility

modifiers.name: Borgohain Governance
modifiers.text: The seven great offices transplanted into Bengal, ruling through the existing zamindari nobility: slower mobilization but smoother absorption of the conquered country.

destiny.name: The Swargadeo's Imperium
destiny.text: Pandua bows, the Burmese frontier breaks at Pinya and Sagaing. The Tai mandate now reaches from the Patkai to the lower Ganges. Charaideo, the first capital and the burial ground of the kings, is rebuilt to twice its old size, and the imperial court there fuses Charaideo dynastic legitimacy with Sanskritic Bengal high culture.

conditions.text: Own Pandua, or a subject owns it
Own Pinya, or a subject owns it
Own Sagaing, or a subject owns it
Prestige at least 75
Charaideo is ours and has reached 43 development

event.title: The Imperial Court at Charaideo
event.text: Pandua submits, Pinya falls, Sagaing's monasteries open their gates. The Swargadeo's banner now flies over a continental imperium reaching from the Burmese hills to the Ganges floodplain. The court at Charaideo is rebuilt as an imperial seat: Sanskritic ceremonial fused to Tai dynastic ritual, Buranji chronicles fused to Persian court historiography. The Borphukan asks the Swargadeo where the realm now turns: continental consolidation, or further into the eastern frontier?

modifiers.name: Swargadeo's Imperium
modifiers.text: Charaideo rebuilt as an imperial seat, garrisons knit across the continent, the Buranjis revised to record a kingdom reaching from the Patkai to the lower Ganges.

options.text: Push further east: break the Burmese frontier

modifiers.name: Burmese Frontier
modifiers.text: The Patkai crossed in the other direction. Riverine fleets on the Irrawaddy, paik garrisons in the dry zone, the Tai dragoons riding the upper Burma plain.

destiny.name: The Satras Embraced
destiny.text: Sankardev's reform crosses into the wider eastern world. With silk traded through the kingdom's market, the satras become a network reaching beyond the valley, and Bordowa, where Sankardev was born and raised his first prayer hall, grows into its mother house: build it up, and raise a temple or a Namghar there.

conditions.text: Chose Sankardev's Eka-Sarana dharma
Our Bordowa has a Temple or a Namghar
The capital

children.text: Silk is produced in the market
Silk is traded in the market

conditions.text: Bordowa is ours and has reached 21 development

event.title: The Satras Reach Outward
event.text: Muga silk passes through the satra workshops and out to the markets of the wider world; the scribes of the satras copy the Bhagavata Purana in Assamese onto leaves of sanchi bark, and the copies are read aloud to lay hearers across the eastern marches. Sankardev's bhakti reform (once a movement of the upper Brahmaputra) now reaches into the Sundarbans and the hill kingdoms beyond. The namghars are beginning to network.

destiny.name: The Bay-Coast Pilgrimage
destiny.text: Take Chittagong and Khulna, plant satras on the Sundarbans coast, and bind the river-mouths into the Vaishnava network. With a dry dock or a greater yard at Chittagong and a treasury of two thousand gold, the devotional federation reaches the sea.

conditions.text: Own Chittagong, or a subject owns it
Own Khulna, or a subject owns it
Our Chittagong has a Dry Dock, Shipyard, Grand Shipyard or Naval Base
Gold at least 2000

event.title: The Sundarbans Open to the Satra
event.text: Chittagong's port and Khulna's tidal forests now answer to the Swargadeo. The satras send their bhakats down the rivers to plant namghars among the Sundarban fisherfolk and the Chittagong rice planters. The satradhikars debate how the new network should be governed: as a council of equal satras meeting in pilgrimage on the coast, or as a popular Eka-Sarana movement spreading without hierarchy among ordinary villagers?

options.text: Form the satra council on the Bay coast

modifiers.name: Satra Diplomacy
modifiers.text: The bhakats serve as envoys; the satras as embassies. Sankardev's reform travels the trade routes of the Bay coast under the Swargadeo's seal.

options.text: Let the namghar movement spread among the people

modifiers.name: Namghar Outreach
modifiers.text: The Eka-Sarana movement runs ahead of the satra hierarchy: namghars in every fishing village, lay devotion among the Sundarban rice planters and the Chittagong coast.

destiny.name: The Pan-Vaishnava Commonwealth
destiny.text: Mrauk-U, Chandrawip, and Pegu joined under the Swargadeo's protection, with at least two kingdoms of the coast ruled as subjects. With three thousand gold in the treasury, the Mahapurusha Mahasattra becomes the seat of a maharaja-of-the-east, sovereign of a Bay-coast Vaishnava commonwealth.

conditions.text: Own Mrauk U, or a subject owns it
Own Chandrawip, or a subject owns it
Own Pegu, or a subject owns it
Num subjects at least 2
Gold at least 3000

event.title: The Maharaja of the East
event.text: Mrauk-U bows, Chandrawip joins, Pegu's Buddhist court accepts the protective sovereignty of the Swargadeo. The Mahapurusha Mahasattra is consecrated as the seat of a Vaishnava commonwealth stretching from the Sundarbans to the Irrawaddy delta. The Swargadeo is hailed as Maharaja of the East. The court asks how this commonwealth should be ordered: through coastal trade and diplomatic ties to the wider Indian Ocean, or through the satra network alone, an inward-facing federation of devotion?

options.text: Open the commonwealth to the Bay trade

modifiers.name: Maharaja of the East
modifiers.text: The Bay-coast commonwealth bound by trade: Chittagong, Mrauk-U, Pegu under the Swargadeo's protective sovereignty, the Indian Ocean envoys arriving at Charaideo.

options.text: Bind the federation through satra alone

modifiers.name: Satra Commonwealth
modifiers.text: An inward-facing federation of namghars and satras stretching from the Brahmaputra to the Irrawaddy, bound by devotion rather than markets: the Mahapurusha lineage as the constitution of the realm.

units.name: Paik Militia
units.text: Corvee-conscripted footmen, the bulk of every Ahom army, armed with khanda blade, hide shield, and matchlock or bow depending on the era.

units.name: Hill Auxiliaries
units.text: Garo, Naga, Bodo, and Kachari fighters under Ahom command, masters of jungle ambush and the broken hill country surrounding the Brahmaputra valley.

units.name: Tai Dragoons
units.text: Mounted infantry of the Ahom court, descendants of the Tai cavalry tradition that crossed the Patkai with Sukaphaa, the elite striking arm of the realm.

units.name: Borphukan's Marines
units.text: Lachit Borphukan's elite naval infantry, victors at Saraighat in 1671 where they boarded and destroyed a Mughal armada on the Brahmaputra.

units.name: Jaibanmar Artillery
units.text: Ahom heavy artillery corps, manning the jaiban cannon and swivel guns that combined Indian and Persian gunnery influences.

units.name: Modern Paltan
units.text: European-drilled line infantry recruited through paik corvee, the modernizing reforms of the late Ahom period to face firearm-equipped foes.

units.name: Assamese Paltan
units.text: Modern line infantry raised through paik recruitment, the synthesis of six centuries of Ahom levy tradition and contemporary military drill.

units.name: Brahmaputra Warship
units.text: Bachari and kosa: light gun-armed riverboats forming the patrol fleet of the Brahmaputra under the Borphukan's command.

buildings.name: Paik Office
buildings.text: Bureau of corvee labor under one of the great offices, organizing the village got of four into the militia, work crews, and revenue base of the kingdom.

buildings.name: Buranji Archive
buildings.text: The court chronicle scriptorium where Tai-Ahom and Assamese-language histories of the kingdom are written, copied, and stored, the documentary memory of the realm.

buildings.name: Charaideo Maidam Complex
buildings.text: The royal mound necropolis where Tai-derived burial tradition continued through six centuries of Ahom kings, the spiritual heart of the kingdom.

buildings.name: Namghar
buildings.text: Sankardev's village prayer hall, the institutional core of the Eka-Sarana religion: open hall with central scripture stand, communal recitation, and no caste-restricted sanctum.

buildings.name: Dolakharia Dockyard
buildings.text: The Borphukan's naval headquarters at Guwahati, the river fortress and shipyard from which the Brahmaputra fleet sallies to meet every Mughal incursion.

buildings.name: Satra
buildings.text: Vaishnava monastic complex of the Eka-Sarana lineage: manuscript scriptorium, devotional center, agricultural estate, and political constituency rolled into one institution.

buildings.name: Brahmaputra Industrial Works
buildings.text: Modernized riverbank manufactories combining mill, dockyard, and textile works, late-Ahom and post-restoration industrial infrastructure on the Brahmaputra.

buildings.name: Imperial Court
buildings.text: The capstone of Path A: a Tai-Hindu syncretic court combining Charaideo dynastic ritual with Sanskritic Bengal high culture, seat of the Swargadeo's continental imperium.

buildings.name: Mahapurusha Mahasattra
buildings.text: The capstone of Path B: the great satra of the Mahapurusha lineage, seat of the satradhikar of the pan-Vaishnava commonwealth and node of the Bay-coast namghar network.

buildings.name: Eka-Sarana Workshop
buildings.text: The production-side complement to the satra. Where the monastery copies scripture and runs prayer, the workshop presses Brahmaputra-valley tea leaf into trade-grade chests. A satra-licensed manufactory under sattradhikar oversight.

children.text: Tea is produced in the market

list.name: Patro Mantri Sabha
list.text: The standing council of the Seven Great Offices: the Burhagohain, Borgohain, Borpatrogohain, Borphukan, Borbarua, Bargohain, and the lesser officers. Codified under Suhungmung (r. 1497-1539) and enlarged under Pratap Singha, the Sabha confirmed succession to the Swargadeo's throne and could depose unfit kings. The Ahom polity's constitutional check distinguished it from its Mughal and Bengali neighbors: the Swargadeo ruled with the council, never above it.

list.name: Paik-Khel Administration
list.text: The standing corvee bureau under the Likchau paik-roll keepers. Codified under Momai Tamuli Borbarua (1609), every adult male was enrolled into a got of three or four paiks, each paik owing rotating service to a Khel office. Three paiks supported the fourth in militia or labor service. The system manned the bachari river fleet, built the Brahmaputra embankments, and constituted the standing levy that broke the Mughal armies seventeen times across the seventeenth century.

list.name: Buranji Likchau
list.text: The institutionalized court chronicle apparatus. The Buranjis (the word means 'store of unprecedented things') were written first in the Tai-Ahom script, later in Assamese. A literate scribal corps attended every court session, every embassy, and every campaign, producing one of the great non-imperial chronicle traditions of South Asia. The Buranjis were consulted as legal precedent and diplomatic record into the nineteenth century, an institutional memory the kingdom's neighbors lacked.

list.name: Sattradhikar Mandali
list.text: The institutionalized assembly of Vaishnava monastic authorities, heads of the satras founded under Srimanta Sankardev (1449-1568) and codified by Madhabdev. The great satras (Auniati, Dakhinpat, Garhmur, Kuruwabahi) held crown grants of land in debottar and brahmottar tenure, administered their own cultivators, ran the namghar village congregations, and arbitrated disputes outside the Patra Mantri courts. Eka-Sarana devotion offered the Bodo, Kachari, and other valley peoples a path of integration that Brahmanical Hinduism withheld.

conditions.text: Owns Bordowa
